name: saa7185_write_block
prose: Precondition: data points to len readable bytes forming (register, value) pairs, sd is a valid subdev whose client data and private data (struct saa7185) are set; register numbers are expected to be below 128 because the cache encoder->reg has 128 entries and there is no bounds check. Postcondition: if len < 2 nothing is sent or cached and -1 is returned. If the adapter supports I2C_FUNC_I2C, it groups pairs with consecutive register numbers into one block (the first register byte plus values, at most 32 bytes per block), stores every value of the block into encoder->reg before the block is sent, and sends each block with i2c_master_send; it stops at the first block whose send returns a negative value and returns that error, in which case every pair of that block has already been cached and pairs in later blocks have not; if all blocks succeed it returns the result of the last i2c_master_send, which is the positive byte count of that block. Otherwise (no raw I2C support) it calls saa7185_write for each pair in turn, which caches the value and then does an SMBus byte write; it stops at the first negative result and returns it, with the failing pair already cached and later pairs not, and returns 0 if all writes succeed. A trailing odd byte is ignored.
note: Reviewer 1 right (positive byte count on raw path, -1 for len<2); reviewer 2 right (pairs after a failed transfer are not cached); reviewer 3 right (in block mode all pairs of a failed block are cached before the send, saa7185.c:84-89). New caveat: encoder->reg is only 128 bytes (line 36) and the raw path indexes it with an unchecked u8 register. saa7185.c:65-105.

name: tc358743_probe_of
prose: Precondition: state points to a tc358743_state whose i2c_client is set; this describes the CONFIG_OF definition (tc358743.c:2007-2162). With CONFIG_OF disabled the file instead defines a stub tc358743_probe_of that only returns -ENODEV and does not touch state. Postcondition: it gets the clock named refclk with devm_clk_get (an error is returned through dev_err_probe), finds endpoint 0 in the device-tree graph (returns -EINVAL if there is none), parses it with v4l2_fwnode_endpoint_alloc_parse (its error is returned) and returns -EINVAL if the bus type is not CSI-2 D-PHY, there are no data lanes or no link frequencies, or if there are more than 4 lanes. It then copies the CSI-2 bus settings into state->bus, enables the clock with clk_prepare_enable (its error is returned), and fills state->pdata: refclk_hz from clk_get_rate, ddc5v_delay, enable_hdcp false, fifo_level 374, pll_prd derived from refclk_hz only for 26, 27 and 42 MHz, bps per lane as twice the first link frequency (returns -EINVAL and disables the clock if it is outside 62.5 Mbps to 1 Gbps), pll_fbd and the lane timing counters for 594 or 972 Mbps (any other rate uses the 594 Mbps values with a warning). For a refclk rate other than 26, 27 or 42 MHz it logs an error and jumps to the clock-disable exit with ret still holding 0 from clk_prepare_enable, so in that case the clock is disabled again and the function returns 0 with the later pdata fields not filled in. It then gets the optional reset GPIO into state->reset_gpio (an error disables the clock and is returned) and, if the GPIO exists, pulses it through tc358743_gpio_reset. On success it returns 0 with the reference clock left enabled. On every path after the endpoint was found the endpoint is freed with v4l2_fwnode_endpoint_free (once it was parsed) and the node reference is dropped with of_node_put.
note: Reviewer 3 right: the real implementation dereferences state and returns 0 or error codes; the old prose described only the CONFIG_OF-off stub (tc358743.c:2163-2167). Slice is inside the real function at 2007-2162. Notable: unsupported refclk path (2081-2084) goes to disable_clk with ret == 0, i.e. returns success. Both definitions are in the file; I documented the real one and mention the stub.

name: __media_entity_setup_link
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the media device graph mutex (this function takes no lock); link is NULL or a valid media_link whose source, sink and reverse pointers are valid, and flags is the requested link flags. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if link is NULL, or if flags differs from link->flags in any bit other than MEDIA_LNK_FL_ENABLED. If link->flags has MEDIA_LNK_FL_IMMUTABLE it returns 0 when link->flags equals flags and -EINVAL otherwise; if link->flags already equals flags it returns 0; in these equal cases nothing is modified. It returns -EBUSY if the link does not have MEDIA_LNK_FL_DYNAMIC and either its source pad or its sink pad is streaming. If the media device has ops->link_notify it calls it with MEDIA_DEV_NOTIFY_PRE_LINK_CH and returns its result at once if negative (no flags changed, no post notification); a non-negative result is ignored. It then calls __media_entity_setup_link_notify, which calls the source entity's link_setup and, if that returns a negative value other than -ENOIOCTLCMD, returns it with no restore call and no change to link->flags; otherwise it calls the sink entity's link_setup and, if that returns a negative value other than -ENOIOCTLCMD, calls the source entity's link_setup again with the old link->flags and returns the sink error with link->flags unchanged; if both are accepted (or lack the operation) it sets link->flags and link->reverse->flags to flags and returns 0. After that call, if the media device has ops->link_notify, it calls it with MEDIA_DEV_NOTIFY_POST_LINK_CH and the requested flags whether or not the setup succeeded, ignoring its return value, and returns the result of __media_entity_setup_link_notify.
note: Reviewer 4 right: the source-entity restore call happens only when the sink's link_setup fails (mc-entity.c:1297-1302); a source failure returns directly (1294-1295). Reviewers 1 and 3 right (POST notify called even on failure, return ignored, 1349-1351; equal returns do not touch reverse->flags). Reviewer 'mechanical' about contract only.

name: set_audclk_freq
prose: Precondition: cx points to an initialized cx18 device (cx->av_state readable and the audio/video chip registers writable through cx18_av_write and cx18_av_write4); freq is any u32. Postcondition: if freq is not 32000, 44100 or 48000 it returns -EINVAL with no register written and state->audclk_freq unchanged. Otherwise it programs the VID_PLL and AUX_PLL fractions, the sample-rate converter control registers, the MCLK select and divider and the audio and video counters, using one register set when state->aud_input is greater than CX18_AV_AUDIO_SERIAL2 and a different register set otherwise, with values chosen by freq (three cases in each set); it then sets state->audclk_freq to freq and returns 0. Register write failures are not checked. No locks are taken.
note: Prose was accurate (cx18-av-audio.c:13-287; both branches switch on 32000/44100/48000 and fall to the common audclk_freq store at line 283). Mechanical reviewer complaint concerned the old formal contract only; contract field set to empty because the function writes device registers and device state (rule 4). Not read: the individual register constants of the six register sets.

name: cx23885_gpio_setup
prose: Precondition: dev points to an initialized cx23885_dev whose board field is set and whose GPIO registers are accessible (through the cx_set, cx_clear and cx_write register macros and the cx23885_gpio_enable, cx23885_gpio_clear and cx23885_gpio_set helpers). Postcondition: this is cx23885_gpio_setup, a void function with no error returns. It switches on dev->board; for each of the listed board constants (there is no default case) it applies that board's GPIO and reset-line setup: typically setting or clearing bits in registers such as GP0_IO, pulsing the reset lines of demodulators and tuners, or enabling GPIO pins, with sleeps of between 5 ms and 200 ms between steps on many boards; some boards (for example the ViewCast 260e and 460e) are listed only to document that no GPIO setup is needed. For a board value not listed it does nothing. It does not write any field of dev, allocates nothing, takes no locks and reports no status; register write results are not checked.
note: Not a drop: slice 1734-1991 is the middle and end of cx23885_gpio_setup (cx23885-cards.c:1542-1961); name was not visible in the excerpt. I read the beginning, the last two cases and a structural summary of the whole switch (53 case labels, no dev field assignments, no default), but not every case body, so the prose deliberately stays at the level of what the cases have in common.

name: cx25821_video_register
prose: Precondition: dev points to an initialized cx25821_dev whose channels, SRAM channel tables, video_nr entry and PCI device are set up. Postcondition: this is cx25821_video_register. It sets dev->tvnorm to V4L2_STD_NTSC_M, initialises dev->slock, and loops over channel indexes 0 up to MAX_VID_CAP_CHANNEL_NUM - 2, skipping SRAM_CH08 (the audio channel). For input channels (index not above SRAM_CH08) it initialises a control handler with brightness, contrast, saturation and hue controls and runs v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup; for output channels it links the channel to dev->vid_out_data. It then fills in the channel's SRAM channel, width 720, interlaced field, height 576 or 480 by dev->tvnorm, pixel format, clears the interrupt status, initialises the vb2 queue fields (calling vb2_queue_init only for input channels), fills in and names the video device and registers it with video_register_device. If any of the handler error check, handler setup, vb2_queue_init or video_register_device fails for index i, it jumps to fail_unreg, which calls cx25821_video_unregister for i, i-1, ..., 0 in that order and returns the error code. cx25821_video_unregister clears bit 0 of PCI_INT_MSK and, only for channels whose video device is registered, unregisters it and frees its control handler; a channel whose control handler was initialised but whose device was not registered (for example the failing channel itself) has its handler not freed here. If all channels register, it sets PCI_INT_MSK to 0xff and returns 0.
note: Not a drop: slice 765-774 is the tail of cx25821_video_register (cx25821-video.c:665-776); the old prose was right about the tail but the listed item is the real function, so FIX under its real name. Registered indexes below the failing one include skipped channel SRAM_CH08, for which unregister is a no-op for a device that was never registered. Read the whole function.

name: dvb_register
prose: Precondition: dev points to a valid cx8802_dev whose core, frontends container and pci device are initialized. Postcondition: this is dvb_register. It starts with res = -EINVAL. If core->i2c_rc is non-zero it logs and goes to frontend_detach, and if vb2_dvb_get_frontend(&dev->frontends, 1) returns NULL it also goes to frontend_detach, in both cases with res still -EINVAL. Otherwise it sets dev->frontends.gate to 0 and core->gate_ctrl to cx88_dvb_gate_ctrl and switches on core->boardnr to attach the demodulator and tuner for that board (some boards also set dev->ts_gen_cntrl, pulse GPIO lines, install board-specific callbacks or ops such as set_voltage, set_params or i2c_gate_ctrl, and for the two-frontend boards such as HVR4000 fetch the second frontend with vb2_dvb_get_frontend(..., 2), set mfe_shared and attach a second demodulator); a failing tuner attach or missing second frontend in a case goes to frontend_detach with res -EINVAL; an unsupported board only logs and falls out of the switch. If fe0's frontend (or fe1's, when used) is NULL after the switch it logs and goes to frontend_detach with res -EINVAL. Otherwise it sets the frontend callback to cx88_tuner_callback and ts_bus_ctrl to cx88_dvb_bus_ctrl (for fe1 too if present), puts the tuner in standby with call_all, and calls vb2_dvb_register_bus; if that returns non-zero it goes to frontend_detach with res set to its return value; if it returns 0 the function returns 0. frontend_detach sets core->gate_ctrl to NULL, calls vb2_dvb_dealloc_frontends on dev->frontends and returns res. There is no -ENODEV or -ENOMEM return in this function.
note: Reviewer 4 right: no -ENOMEM path and a missing first frontend returns -EINVAL. The old prose also claimed -ENODEV for i2c_rc != 0 and for failed attaches, which is wrong: res is initialised to -EINVAL and only vb2_dvb_register_bus assigns res (cx88-dvb.c:986-1641, 'res =' only at line 991 (initialiser) and at the vb2_dvb_register_bus call near 1630). The slice cut the head; real function is dvb_register. I read the head, the tail, the returns/gotos/res assignments and the HVR4000/second-frontend cases but not every board case body.

name: cx8800_initdev
prose: Precondition: pci_dev is a PCI device being probed by this driver; the function allocates its own cx8800_dev, so no other state is required from the caller. Postcondition: kzalloc failure returns -ENOMEM with nothing else done. pci_enable_device failure returns -EIO after only kfree(dev) (it does not touch the core or disable the device). cx88_core_get returning NULL returns -EINVAL after pci_disable_device and kfree(dev). dma_set_mask failure and request_irq failure (negative) unwind through fail_core: they set core->v4ldev to NULL, drop the core reference with cx88_core_put, call pci_disable_device and kfree(dev) and return the error. A failing audio or video control creation (v4l2_ctrl_new_std returning NULL) returns that handler's error after free_irq and the same fail_core steps. Otherwise, after creating the controls it optionally adds the wm8775, tvaudio and (for some DVICO boards) rtc subdevices and modules, calls pci_set_drvdata(pci_dev, dev) and sets core->v4ldev to dev, takes core->lock, sets the TV norm, runs v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup on both handlers (results ignored), initialises the video and VBI vb2 queues, and registers the video and VBI device nodes, and a radio device node when core->board.radio.type is CX88_RADIO. A failure of vb2_queue_init or of any video_register_device goes through fail_unreg: cx8800_unregister_video(dev), release of core->lock, then the free_irq and fail_core steps, and the error is returned. If every step succeeds and the board has a tuner it starts the tvaudio kthread; a kthread_run failure is only logged (core->kthread keeps the error pointer) and does not change the result. It then releases core->lock and returns 0. On the failure paths after pci_set_drvdata the driver data of pci_dev is not cleared.
note: Reviewer 4 right: pci_enable_device failure only kfrees dev (cx88-video.c:1270-1273, fail_free), it does not clear v4ldev, call cx88_core_put or pci_disable_device. Old prose also left out -ENOMEM and the pci_set_drvdata-not-cleared detail. Slice cut the head; function at 1255-1521, read fully. Observation: core->kthread keeps an ERR_PTR value if kthread_run fails (1498-1502).

name: ddb_redirect
prose: Precondition: the caller does not hold redirect_lock; i and p select entries of the global ddbs array via (i >> 4) & 0x3f and (p >> 4) & 0x3f, an input index (i & 7) and a port index (p & 0x0f) that are in range for those devices. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if either selected ddbs entry is NULL or either device lacks has_dma, or if the selected port (pdev->port[p & 0x0f]) has no output. It then calls ddb_unredirect(port), which takes redirect_lock itself and returns -EBUSY (without changing anything) if the port's output DMA is running, and otherwise removes any existing redirection of that port; a non-zero result makes this function return -EBUSY. If i is 8 it returns 0 at this point, having only undone the port's previous redirection. Otherwise it takes input = &idev->input[i & 7] (the NULL test that follows can never be true for an array element, so its -EINVAL return is not reachable in practice), takes redirect_lock, and returns -EBUSY after releasing it if the port output's DMA or the input's DMA is running. Otherwise, with the lock held, if port->input[0] exists it sets that input's redi to input->redi and clears input->redi when input->redi was non-NULL, or sets it to input when it was NULL; it sets input->redo to port->output and port->output->redi to input, calls ddb_redirect_dma(input->port->dev, input->dma, port->output->dma), which copies the output DMA's buffer value and writes its buffer addresses to the input DMA's buffer registers, releases the lock and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 2 right (the input NULL check at ddb_redirect line 240-241 exists but is dead for an array element); reviewer 3 wrong: ddb_redirect_dma IS called at line 260 and copies bufval and the buffer table registers (160-174). Old prose had the order wrong: ddb_unredirect runs after the -EINVAL checks (233), not first. ddbridge-core.c:218-263.

name: __ipu6_mmu_map
prose: Precondition: mmu_info points to an initialized ipu6_mmu_info; size is a multiple of ISP_PAGE_SIZE (l2_map decrements size by whole pages while size > 0); the caller holds no mmu_info->lock (it is taken inside l2_map). Postcondition: it rounds iova down to ISP_PAGE_SIZE (the computed end address is used only in a debug message) and returns the result of l2_map(mmu_info, round_down(iova), paddr, size). l2_map takes mmu_info->lock with spin_lock_irqsave and aligns paddr up to ISP_PAGE_SIZE. For each L1 index from the iova's index while size > 0 and the index is below ISP_L1PT_PTES it ensures an L2 page table exists (allocating a zeroed page with GFP_ATOMIC | GFP_DMA32 filled with the dummy page entry, if the L2 entry is still the dummy and no table is cached, and DMA-mapping it) and writes one L2 entry per page, consuming size, then flushes the cache lines. It returns 0 after the loop, and the loop stops without error when the L1 index reaches ISP_L1PT_PTES even if size is still above 0, so 0 does not by itself prove the whole size was mapped. It returns -ENOMEM if the L2 page table allocation fails and -EINVAL if map_single of the L2 page table fails (it frees the page it had in hand in that case); on either error it releases the lock and calls l2_unmap on the pages it had already mapped before returning the error.
note: Reviewer 1 right (maps only size bytes from round_down(iova); iova_end is used only for debug); reviewer 2 right (l2_map aligns paddr up, ipu6-mmu.c:322); reviewer 3 right (map_single failure returns -EINVAL, 340-345; allocation failure returns -ENOMEM, 334-336). Extra: the l1 loop can end with size > 0 and still return 0 (323-324, 384). Also on map_single failure free_page is applied to l2_virt even if that table was an existing cached l2_pts entry (343), not noted in the prose. __ipu6_mmu_map at 395-406, l2_map at 306-393.

name: ipu6_pci_probe
prose: Precondition: called by the PCI core with a valid pdev and the matching pci_device_id id; the device ID need not be a supported one. Postcondition: it allocates the ipu6_device with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure), enables the PCI device and maps BAR0 with the pcim helpers (their errors are returned), sets drvdata and bus mastering, and selects hw_ver and the firmware name from id->device, returning -ENODEV for an ID that is not one of the listed IPU6 IDs (after drvdata and bus mastering were already set; devm resources are released by the core). It sets the 39-bit DMA mask (error returned), runs ipu6_pci_config_setup and ipu6_buttress_init; a failure of any of these steps up to and including ipu6_buttress_init returns directly with no unwind. It then requests the CPD firmware (failure goes to buttress_exit, which only calls ipu6_buttress_exit), validates it, duplicates the isys and psys buttress control structures (-ENOMEM on failure), creates the isys and psys auxiliary devices, takes a runtime-PM reference on the psys device with pm_runtime_resume_and_get, initialises the psys MMU hardware, maps the firmware image, creates the package directory, and requests the shared threaded IRQ with devm_request_threaded_irq; a failure after the firmware request unwinds through the labels out_free_irq (devm_free_irq, used only when authentication fails), out_ipu6_rpm_put (pm_runtime_put_sync on the psys device, not used when the runtime-PM get itself failed) and out_ipu6_bus_del_devices, which frees the package directory and unmaps the firmware image whenever isp->psys is valid (whether or not those steps had completed), cleans up the psys and isys MMUs when they exist, deletes the bus devices, releases the firmware and calls ipu6_buttress_exit, and then returns the error. After a successful ipu6_buttress_authenticate it cleans up the psys MMU hardware, drops the psys runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_put, configures the VC arbitration, logs the hardware version, calls pm_runtime_put_noidle and pm_runtime_allow on the PCI device, sets isp->bus_ready_to_probe to true and returns 0.
note: Reviewer right: unsupported IDs return -ENODEV (ipu6.c:550-553), so the old precondition 'ID must be supported' was wrong. Slice cut the head: real function ipu6_pci_probe at 492-697. Extra detail: failures between the firmware map and package-dir steps still run ipu6_cpd_free_pkg_dir and ipu6_buttress_unmap_fw_image in the shared unwind (683-686). I read the full function.

name: ivtv_start_v4l2_encode_stream
prose: Precondition: s points to a valid ivtv_stream of an initialized ivtv device (itv = s->itv); the caller holds no lock this function needs (it takes none). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL with no change if s->vdev.v4l2_dev is NULL or if s->type is not IVTV_ENC_STREAM_TYPE_MPG, YUV, PCM or VBI. For the accepted types it chooses the capture type and subtype; for MPG it also turns passthrough mode off if itv->output_mode is OUT_PASSTHROUGH (remembering to turn it back on) and resets itv->mpg_data_received, vbi_data_inserted, the dual-watch fields and search_pack_header; for VBI it resets the itv->vbi frame counters and sliced size array. It sets s->subtype, clears s->buffers_stolen and clears IVTV_F_S_STREAMOFF. If itv->capturing is 0 it then programs the encoder (DMA block size, crop line, misc settings, placeholder, vsync lines by digitizer type, VBI setup if V4L2_CAP_VBI_CAPTURE, program index info, handler setup, optional radio mute) and, further below, sets the capture IRQ mask, clears IVTV_F_I_EOS, marks the control handler busy and restarts the audio and video digitizer streaming after a 300 ms wait. Independent of itv->capturing, on a cx23415 whose IVTV_F_I_DIG_RST flag was not yet set it sets the flag, enables the VIM-reset event notification and clears that IRQ mask bit. It then issues CX2341X_ENC_START_CAPTURE; if that firmware command returns non-zero it returns -EINVAL, leaving all the changes above in place (including passthrough turned off) and itv->capturing unchanged. On success it re-enables passthrough if it had been turned off, clears the VBI capture IRQ mask bit for a VBI stream or the capture IRQ mask otherwise, increments itv->capturing and returns 0. There is no early return for an already streaming stream in this function.
note: Reviewer 2 right (encoder/VBI/digitizer setup only when itv->capturing == 0, ivtv-streams.c:533 and 601). Reviewers 1 and 3 wrong: there is no early 'return 0 if IVTV_F_S_STREAMING already set' in ivtv_start_v4l2_encode_stream (474-641); the only returns are -EINVAL at 482, 525, 625 and 0 at 640. Slice cut the head. Read the whole function.

name: ngene_command_mutex
prose: Precondition: dev and com are valid; dev->FWInterfaceBuffer, dev->ngenetohost, dev->cmd_wq, dev->cmd_lock, dev->pci_dev and the register mappings are initialised; com->in_len + 2 bytes fit in dev->FWInterfaceBuffer (and in the host-to-device window if BootFirmware is set) and com->out_len bytes (plus one when out_len is 0) fit in dev->ngenetohost; the caller serialises command use (ngene_command takes dev->cmd_mutex around this function). Postcondition: it first sets dev->cmd_done to 0. If the opcode is CMD_FWLOAD_PREPARE it sets dev->BootFirmware to 1, records dev->icounts from NGENE_INT_COUNTS and writes 0 to the command, status and event registers (both halves); if the opcode is CMD_FWLOAD_FINISH it writes the addresses dev->PAFWInterfaceBuffer, +256 and +512 to the command, status and event registers. It copies com->in_len + 2 bytes of com->cmd.raw8 into dev->FWInterfaceBuffer and, if dev->BootFirmware is non-zero, also copies them to the device with ngcpyto. Under dev->cmd_lock (spin_lock_irq) it sets dev->CmdDoneByte to ngenetohost + out_len (one byte further if out_len is 0), clears that byte and the first two bytes of dev->ngenetohost, and releases the lock. It writes 1 to FORCE_INT and waits up to 2 seconds for dev->cmd_done to be 1. On timeout it logs an error, dumps the command I/O and returns -1 without touching dev->prev_cmd or the output buffer; dev->BootFirmware is then still 1 after a CMD_FWLOAD_PREPARE and unchanged from its value at entry otherwise. On success it clears dev->BootFirmware if the opcode was CMD_FWLOAD_FINISH, sets dev->prev_cmd to the opcode, copies com->out_len bytes from dev->ngenetohost into com->cmd.raw8 when out_len is non-zero, and returns 0.
note: Reviewers 1 and 3 right (dev->cmd_done is cleared at entry, ngene-core.c:260, before the opcode handling); reviewer 2 right (on timeout BootFirmware is unchanged for FWLOAD_FINISH, 309-310 only on success). ngene_command_mutex at 254-320 (ngene_command wraps it with cmd_mutex at 322-330).

name: saa7134_board_init2
prose: Precondition: dev points to a valid, already probed saa7134_dev whose board, tuner_type, tda9887_conf, eedata, i2c_adap, i2c_client, v4l2_dev, insuspend and autodetected fields are initialised. Postcondition: it switches on dev->board and for the listed boards runs board-specific fixups, which can rewrite dev->board, dev->tuner_type, dev->tda9887_conf and dev->has_remote (for example the BMK MPEX, MD7134, Europa/Tiger, ASUS, VideoMate T200 and FlyDVB Trio boards) and issue I2C transfers or GPIO writes whose failures are only logged or ignored; boards not listed get no fixup. Then, only if dev->insuspend is false and dev->tuner_type is not TUNER_ABSENT, it registers the radio tuner (if dev->radio_type is set), the demodulator (if the TDA9887 is present) and the TV tuner I2C subdevices on dev->i2c_adap. Whether or not that registration was done, it then calls saa7134_tuner_setup(dev) and, for the boards BEHOLD_COLUMBUS_TVFM and AVERMEDIA_CARDBUS_501, sets dev->i2c_client.addr to 0xC0 and sends a TEA5767 configuration with saa_call_all. It has a single return, which is 0 at the end; there is no error return.
note: Reviewer right: saa7134_tuner_setup(dev) and the TEA5767 configuration are outside the 'if (!dev->insuspend && tuner_type != TUNER_ABSENT)' block (saa7134-cards.c:8070-8118 area, calls after the closing brace). The function is saa7134_board_init2 (7753-8126); I read the start, the later cases and the tail and a list of every case and field assignment, but not every I2C byte in the board cases, so the prose stays summary-level.

name: saa7134_irq
prose: Precondition: dev_id points to a valid, initialised saa7134_dev whose registers are mapped; called as an interrupt handler. Postcondition: if dev->insuspend is set it returns IRQ_NONE without reading a register. Otherwise it loops at most 10 times: each pass reads SAA7134_IRQ_REPORT and SAA7134_IRQ_STATUS, removes the DONE_RA3 bit from the report if dev->dmasound.priv_data is non-NULL, and if the resulting report is 0 it leaves the loop. When the report is non-zero it sets handled to 1, writes the report back to SAA7134_IRQ_REPORT and dispatches: video signal change for RDCAP or INTL; video done for DONE_RA0 when (status & 0x60) == 0; VBI done for DONE_RA0 when (status & 0x40) == 0x40; TS done for DONE_RA2 on cards with MPEG (the mops irq_ts_done callback if present, else saa7134_irq_ts_done); and, for GPIO16 or GPIO18, saa7134_input_irq only when dev->has_remote is SAA7134_REMOTE_GPIO, dev->remote exists and its key mask includes the corresponding bit. It returns IRQ_RETVAL(handled): IRQ_NONE if it never found a non-zero report (insuspend, or a zero report after masking DONE_RA3 on the first pass, in which case nothing is acknowledged), and IRQ_HANDLED once any pass acknowledged a report, including when a later pass found no more work. If all 10 passes had a non-zero report it additionally logs the status and, based on the last report, clears the PE enable bit, or the GPIO16 enable bits, or the GPIO18 enable bits in SAA7134_IRQ2 (first match in that order), and otherwise writes 0 to SAA7134_IRQ1 and SAA7134_IRQ2, with a warning each time. No locks are taken in this function.
note: Reviewer right: IRQ_NONE also results when the report becomes zero after DONE_RA3 is masked out on the first pass (saa7134-core.c:515-525); the old prose said only 'first IRQ report read was zero'. Slice cut the head: function at 499-622.

name: saa7134_input_init1
prose: Precondition: dev points to a valid saa7134_dev whose has_remote, board, pci and related fields are initialised. Postcondition: this is saa7134_input_init1. It returns -ENODEV with nothing allocated if dev->has_remote is not SAA7134_REMOTE_GPIO or if the module parameter disable_ir is non-zero. It then switches on dev->board to choose the keymap name (ir_codes), the key, key-down and key-up masks, a polling interval (50 ms for several boards) and whether raw decoding is used; if dev->board matches no listed case ir_codes stays NULL and it prints an error naming the card and returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it allocates the saa7134_card_ir structure with kzalloc and an rc_dev with rc_allocate_device (-ENOMEM if either fails), sets dev->remote to the new structure, stores the masks, polling and raw_decode, fills in the rc_dev fields (open/close callbacks, device and physical names, PCI ids, keymap name, timeouts, and for raw decode the raw driver type and all IR protocols) and registers it with rc_register_device. On a failure of the allocation or of rc_register_device it frees the rc_dev with rc_free_device, sets dev->remote to NULL, frees the ir structure with kfree and returns the error. On success it returns 0 with dev->remote pointing to the new IR state.
note: Not a drop: the slice is inside saa7134_input_init1 (saa7134-input.c:504-829); the packet name saa7134_input_init was not a real function name. The old prose stopped at 'continues with the rest of the initialization' and so described only the front of the function. Read head, the end and the control flow of the 78-case switch, not every board mask value.

name: tvaudio_thread
prose: Precondition: data is the struct saa7134_dev pointer the kthread was created with, with dev->thread, dev->tvnorm and the static mainscan and tvaudio tables usable. Postcondition: the thread function loops until kthread_should_stop() is true and then sets dev->thread.stopped to 1 and returns 0, reaching that exit only from the check right after the sleep at the top of the outer loop (a stop request seen inside a restart path or inside the final polling loop first ends or leaves that inner step and reaches the outer-loop sleep and check). At the top of each outer pass it calls tvaudio_sleep(dev, -1), which waits interruptibly unless scan1 != scan2 or a stop was requested; tvaudio_sleep returns non-zero exactly when dev->thread.scan1 differs from scan2, i.e. a new scan was requested, and not because the sleep was interrupted by a signal. At the restart label it copies scan2 to scan1, clears dev->tvaudio, writes the monitor and FM matrix registers, sets dev->automute if dev->ctl_automute, mutes the input and waits SCAN_INITIAL_DELAY, jumping back to restart whenever tvaudio_sleep or a carrier check sees that a new scan was requested. It counts the mainscan entries whose std matches dev->tvnorm->id; with exactly one it skips the scan, otherwise it measures every candidate with tvaudio_checkcarrier; it then picks the main carrier if the best level is above 2000 and more than 3 times the second best (setting dev->last_carrier and dev->automute to 0), else the last detected carrier, else the default carrier, in the last two cases setting dev->automute to 1. It sets the carrier, finds the matching tvaudio norm by trying the entries with that carrier (waiting SCAN_SUBCARRIER_DELAY for each) and, if one is found, sets its mode, sets mono, stores it in dev->tvaudio and then, every 5 seconds until a new scan is requested or a stop is requested, takes the mode from dev->thread.mode if that is set, or otherwise from the detected result of tvaudio_getstereo, and applies it with tvaudio_setstereo when it differs from the last applied mode. If no norm was found it goes back to the outer loop.
note: Reviewer 1 right (stop leads to done, not restart); reviewer 2 right (tvaudio_sleep returns scan1 != scan2 only, saa7134-tvaudio.c:314); reviewer 3 right (mode comes from tvaudio_getstereo unless dev->thread.mode is set, 592-597). tvaudio_thread at 460-608, tvaudio_sleep at 302-315.

name: solo_p2m_init
prose: Precondition: solo_dev points to a valid, initialised solo_dev whose registers are accessible, whose p2m_dev array has SOLO_NR_P2M entries and whose sys_config and pdev are set. Postcondition: this is solo_p2m_init. For each of the SOLO_NR_P2M channels it initialises the channel mutex and completion, writes its P2M control register to 0 and its config register, and turns on its P2M interrupt. It then sets solo_dev->sdram_size to 0 and tries sizes from the largest to the smallest (i = 2, 1, 0): for each it writes SOLO_DMA_CTRL with that size, resets the chip by writing SOLO_SYS_CFG with and without SOLO_SYS_CFG_RESET, and runs solo_p2m_test (one test for sizes 1 and 0, two for size 2) and keeps the first size for which the tests return 0, setting solo_dev->sdram_size to (32 MiB << i). If no size passes it logs an error and returns -EIO with sdram_size left at 0. If the detected size is smaller than SOLO_SDRAM_END(solo_dev) it logs an error and returns -EIO with sdram_size set to the detected value. Otherwise it returns 0. The register writes and channel initialisation have been done in all cases. No lock is held on return and nothing is allocated that the caller must release (solo_p2m_test allocates and frees its own test buffers).
note: Not a drop: the slice is the body of solo_p2m_init (solo6x10-p2m.c:250-317); packet name unnamed. Old prose matched the code. solo_p2m_test (called here) allocates and frees its buffers per its own tail at 243-247, which I read only at the end.

name: philips_su1278_ty_ci_tuner_set_params
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid dvb_frontend whose dvb->priv points to a valid budget structure (with i2c_adap) and whose dtv_property_cache holds the requested frequency and symbol rate. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL without touching the hardware if the frequency is below 950000 or above 2150000. Otherwise it computes div = (frequency + 124) / 125 and fills a 4-byte message for I2C address 0x61: byte 0 is bits 8-14 of div, byte 1 is the low byte of div, byte 2 is 0x80 | ((div & 0x18000) >> 10) | 4, and byte 3 is 0x20, with bit 0 set if the symbol rate is below 4000000 and with band bits chosen from the frequency (none below 1250000, 0x40 below 1550000, 0x80 below 2050000, 0xC0 below 2150000; a frequency of exactly 2150000 gets no band bits). It calls fe->ops.i2c_gate_ctrl(fe, 1) if that callback exists (its result is ignored and the gate is not closed here), then sends the message with i2c_transfer and returns -EIO if the transfer does not report exactly one message, or 0 otherwise. No locks or references are taken.
note: Reviewers 1 and 2 right (-EINVAL out of range, -EIO on transfer failure). Reviewer 3 wrong: the symbol rate is used (buf[3] |= 1 when symbol_rate < 4000000, budget-av.c:510-511). Extra: frequency == 2150000 gets no band bits (519-520). Function at 493-527.

name: philips_tdm1316l_tuner_set_params
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid dvb_frontend whose dvb->priv is a valid budget_ci with an initialised i2c adapter and tuner_pll_address, and whose dtv_property_cache holds the frequency and bandwidth_hz; the caller holds no lock. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL, before any I2C access, if p->frequency + 36130000 is below 87000000 or at least 895000000 (charge-pump selection), or if p->frequency is below 49000000 or at least 861000000 (band selection). It then switches on p->bandwidth_hz: for 6000000, 7000000 or 8000000 it writes demodulator register 0x0C through tda1004x_writereg (0x14, 0x80 and 0x14 respectively, result ignored) and selects the filter bit; any other bandwidth returns -EINVAL without that write. It computes the divisor from the frequency, fills a 4-byte tuner message for budget_ci->tuner_pll_address (divisor high and low bytes, 0xca, and charge pump, filter and band bits), calls fe->ops.i2c_gate_ctrl(fe, 1) if it exists (result ignored, gate not closed here) and sends the message with i2c_transfer; it returns -EIO if the transfer does not report exactly one message, otherwise it sleeps 1 ms and returns 0. The demodulator register 0x0C write remains done if the later transfer fails. No locks, references or memory are acquired or released.
note: Reviewer right: the checks are on p->frequency directly (budget-ci.c:739-773) and the old prose's remark about -EINVAL for a bad bandwidth 'after possibly writing demod register 0x0C' was wrong: the default case (792-793) returns before any write; the write happens only for 6, 7 and 8 MHz. Function at 729-813 (slice cut the head).

name: v4l2_pixelformat_to_mcu_format
prose: Precondition: none; pixelformat may be any u32 value. Postcondition: returns 0x188 (0x100 | 0x88, the AL_420_8BITS NV12 8-bit code) when pixelformat equals V4L2_PIX_FMT_NV12 (0x3231564E), and returns (u32)-EINVAL, i.e. 4294967274, for every other value. It reads no state, takes no locks and acquires no references.
note: Prose and contract match the source (allegro-core.c:1026-1035: switch with one case NV12 returning 0x100|0x88, default returning -EINVAL from a u32 function; V4L2_PIX_FMT_NV12 = 'N','V','1','2' = 0x3231564E). The earlier rejections were mechanical complaints about the formal contract only; the contract kept here includes the -EINVAL branch. Slice cut the head.

name: nal_h264_profile
prose: Precondition: profile is any value of enum v4l2_mpeg_video_h264_profile (it is passed as an int-sized enum). Postcondition: returns 66 for V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_PROFILE_BASELINE, 77 for V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_PROFILE_MAIN, 88 for V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_PROFILE_EXTENDED, 100 for V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_PROFILE_HIGH, and -EINVAL (-22) for any other value, including V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_PROFILE_CONSTRAINED_BASELINE; it has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires -2147483648 <= profile <= 2147483647; ensures result == 66 || result == 77 || result == 88 || result == 100 || result == -22; */
note: Matches nal-h264.h:202-217 (static inline, switch of four cases, default -EINVAL). The 'still-rejected' reasons were mechanical complaints about an older contract that omitted -EINVAL; the contract kept here includes -22. Packet slice 1-266 covers the header; the functions are at lines 202 and 227.

name: nal_h264_level
prose: Precondition: level is any value of enum v4l2_mpeg_video_h264_level (passed as an int-sized enum). Postcondition: returns 10 for V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_LEVEL_1_0, 9 for LEVEL_1B, 11 for 1_1, 12 for 1_2, 13 for 1_3, 20 for 2_0, 21 for 2_1, 22 for 2_2, 30 for 3_0, 31 for 3_1, 32 for 3_2, 40 for 4_0, 41 for 4_1, 42 for 4_2, 50 for 5_0, 51 for 5_1, and -EINVAL (-22) for any other value (for example levels above 5_1); it has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires -2147483648 <= level <= 2147483647; ensures result == 9 || result == 10 || result == 11 || result == 12 || result == 13 || result == 20 || result == 21 || result == 22 || result == 30 || result == 31 || result == 32 || result == 40 || result == 41 || result == 42 || result == 50 || result == 51 || result == -22; */
note: Matches nal-h264.h:227-262 (16 cases then default -EINVAL). Mechanical rejections concerned an older contract only.

name: vpu_core_resume
prose: Precondition: dev is the device of a vpu core whose drvdata is a valid struct vpu_core with valid core->vpu, core->lock, workqueue and instance list; the caller does not hold core->lock. Postcondition: it takes core->lock, calls pm_runtime_resume_and_get(dev) with the result ignored (so a runtime-PM reference is held only if that call succeeded), and calls vpu_core_get_vpu(core), which takes a reference on the vpu and on its encoder or decoder count according to core->type and is not released by this function. If core->request_count is non-zero it calls vpu_core_boot(core, false) when the interface reports no power state, or vpu_core_sw_reset(core) otherwise; if that returns non-zero it logs 'resume fail' and sets the core state to VPU_CORE_HANG, and that error is the function's return value. It then calls vpu_core_update_state (which may set VPU_CORE_HANG or VPU_CORE_DEINIT from the power state and request count), calls pm_runtime_put_sync(dev) whether or not the get succeeded, and releases core->lock. After unlocking it calls vpu_core_resume_work, which queues the core's message work and delayed message work and, taking core->lock again, queues each instance's message work. It returns 0 if core->request_count is 0 or the boot or reset succeeded, otherwise the non-zero error from vpu_core_boot or vpu_core_sw_reset.
note: Reviewers right: vpu_core_put_vpu is never called (the VPU reference stays, reviewer 2); the result of pm_runtime_resume_and_get is ignored (reviewer 3, vpu_core.c:784) and pm_runtime_put_sync is called unconditionally (798); reviewer 1 right about the request_count error path. The old prose omitted vpu_core_update_state and the post-unlock vpu_core_resume_work details. vpu_core_resume at 778-803.

name: csi2rx_start
prose: Precondition: csi2rx is a valid initialised csi2rx_priv with valid clocks, resets, lane maps, max_streams entries of pixel_clk, pixel_rst and num_pixels, and a source_subdev; the caller holds csi2rx->lock and no stream is running. Postcondition: it enables p_clk with clk_prepare_enable (a failure is returned before anything else is touched), deasserts p_rst, resets the block, optionally sets the error interrupt mask, programs the static configuration register with the lane map, and, if an external DPHY is present, writes the DPHY lane-control register and calls csi2rx_configure_ext_dphy; if that fails it logs the error, disables p_clk and returns the error, leaving the lane-control register and the static configuration programmed, p_rst deasserted and without calling phy_power_off. For each of the max_streams streams it enables the pixel clock (a failure at stream i jumps to the unwind with i streams enabled), deasserts the pixel reset and programs the stream configuration, data-configuration and start registers. It then enables sys_clk (a failure unwinds all the pixel streams as below, and sys_clk is not disabled because it was never enabled), deasserts sys_rst, and calls the source subdev's s_stream(true); if that returns non-zero it disables sys_clk (sys_rst stays deasserted) and then runs the same unwind. The unwind asserts the pixel reset and disables the pixel clock of each enabled stream in reverse order, writes 0 to the DPHY lane-control register and calls phy_power_off if there is a DPHY, and disables p_clk; p_rst is not asserted again on any error path. On success it disables p_clk and returns 0, leaving the pixel clocks and sys_clk enabled and the source streaming. Errors returned are those of the failing call.
note: Reviewer 1 right (configure_ext_dphy failure only disables p_clk: goto err_disable_pclk at cdns-csi2rx.c:361 skips the lane-control clear and phy_power_off at 420-423); reviewers 2 and 3 right (sys_clk enable failure jumps to err_disable_pixclk, 400, so sys_clk is not disabled; old prose said it 'does the same after disabling sys_clk'). Function at 309-428. I did not read csi2rx_configure_ext_dphy, so I make no claim about whether it powers the PHY on.

name: coda_h264_sps_fixup
prose: Precondition: ctx is a valid CODA context, buf holds an H.264 SPS NAL unit (a 5-byte header followed by the RBSP) of *size bytes inside a buffer of max_size bytes, and width and height are the visible dimensions. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL, changing nothing, if *size < 8 or *size >= max_size. It then parses the SPS payload read-only (profile_idc, seq_parameter_set_id, log2_max_frame_num, pic_order_cnt_type with its sub-fields, max_num_ref_frames, the gaps flag, the width and height in macroblocks, frame_mbs_only_flag, the optional mb_adaptive flag, direct_8x8_inference_flag), remembers the bit position of frame_cropping_flag, reads the existing crop offsets if the flag is set and reads vui_parameters_present_flag. It returns -EINVAL if profile_idc is one of 100, 110, 122, 244, 44, 83, 86, 118, 128, 138, 139, 134 or 135 (not implemented, checked right after the seq_parameter_set_id) and -EINVAL if vui_parameters_present_flag is set; a read past the bytes available (the payload is *size - 5 bytes) or an exp-Golomb code with more than 32 leading zeros also returns -EINVAL from the bit reader (not -ENOSPC). If parsing succeeds it computes crop_right = (round_up(width, 16) - width) / 2 and crop_bottom = (round_up(height, 16) - height) / 2 when frame_mbs_only_flag is set, or / 4 when it is not, then rewrites the payload in place from the saved bit position (allowing writes up to max_size - 5 bytes) with frame_cropping_flag = 1, crop_left = 0, crop_right, crop_top = 0, crop_bottom, vui_parameters_present_flag = 0 and a final 1 bit, and sets *size to 5 + ceil(final bit position / 8). A write that would pass max_size - 5 bytes returns -EINVAL with *size unchanged and buf partly rewritten, so the caller must not use buf after any non-zero return from the write stage; a failure during parsing leaves buf unmodified. It returns 0 on success. It takes no locks and keeps no references.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is coda_h264_sps_fixup (coda-h264.c:250-429). Old prose wrongly said -ENOSPC could be returned; the bit readers and writers return only -EINVAL on exhaustion or malformed codes (rbsp_read_bit/rbsp_write_bit, lines 121-144, rbsp_read_bits >32 bits, 146-165). Mechanical reviewer right on the name. Contract left empty (buffer and context arguments).

name: wave5_update_pix_fmt
prose: Precondition: pix_mp points to a v4l2_pix_format_mplane (its pixelformat and, for codec formats, plane_fmt[0].sizeimage already hold valid values), frmsize points to the stepwise frame-size limits, and pix_fmt_type is VPU_FMT_TYPE_CODEC or another type. Postcondition: it first calls v4l2_apply_frmsize_constraints(&width, &height, frmsize), which adjusts the local width and height. If pix_fmt_type is VPU_FMT_TYPE_CODEC it sets pix_mp->width and height to those adjusted values, num_planes to 1, plane_fmt[0].bytesperline to 0 and plane_fmt[0].sizeimage to the larger of DEFAULT_BS_SIZE(width, height) and the previous plane_fmt[0].sizeimage; for any other type it calls v4l2_fill_pixfmt_mp(pix_mp, pix_mp->pixelformat, width, height) to compute the layout. In both cases it then sets pix_mp->flags to 0 and pix_mp->field to V4L2_FIELD_NONE. It returns nothing, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Not a drop: slice 259-271 is the body of wave5_update_pix_fmt (wave5-helper.c:259-278), whose name was cut off; the old prose omitted the frmsize parameter and the constraint step but was otherwise right. FIX under the real name.

name: wave5_vpu_enc_init_seq
prose: Precondition: inst is a valid encoder vpu_instance with an initialised device (inst->dev) and codec_info; the encoder open parameters are read from inst->codec_info->enc_info (its open_param and wave_param), not passed as arguments; inst->std is W_AVC_ENC or W_HEVC_ENC. Postcondition: this is wave5_vpu_enc_init_seq. It computes the rotation/mirror mode word from the instance's rotation_enable, rotation_angle (0, 90, 180 or 270; any other angle adds nothing), mirror_enable and mirror_direction, writes the W5_CMD_ENC_SEQ_* sequence registers with vpu_write_reg (which returns nothing) from the wave parameters, with several registers written differently for W_AVC_ENC and W_HEVC_ENC (SPS/PPS and profile or tier parameters, GOP and intra settings, rate control, intra refresh, conformance window, independent slice mode, and for HEVC only the dependent slice mode and the noise-reduction registers), and zeroes the registers it does not use. The last step is the return statement: it returns the result of send_firmware_command(inst, W5_ENC_SET_PARAM, true, NULL, NULL), i.e. 0 on success or the negative error returned by that command; no other path returns. It takes no locks itself and allocates nothing.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is wave5_vpu_enc_init_seq(inst) (wave5-hw.c:1700-1888), which takes only inst; the old prose invented p_param and p_open_param parameters. I read the beginning, end and every branching construct (switch/if on rotation, mirror and inst->std), not each individual register assignment in the middle. Mechanical reviewer right about the name.

name: mdp_vpu_dev_init
prose: Precondition: vpu is the vpu member of an initialised mdp_dev (so vpu_to_mdp(vpu) and mdp->mdp_data are valid), scp is the SCP device (possibly NULL) and lock points to an initialised mutex the caller does not hold. Postcondition: it initialises vpu->ipi_acked, stores scp and lock in vpu->scp and vpu->lock and sets vpu->work_size to 0. It sends the first SCP_IPI_MDP_INIT message with mdp_vpu_sendmsg, which returns -EINVAL if vpu->scp is NULL or if the acknowledgement left vpu->status non-zero, -EPERM if scp_ipi_send fails, -ETIME if no acknowledgement arrives within the MDP_VPU_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT wait; the ack handler stores the reported work_size in vpu->work_size (when it is still 0) and sets vpu->status even when the status is non-zero, so after a failed first send work_size can be non-zero if an acknowledgement did arrive. If the first send succeeded, under *lock it aligns vpu->work_size to 64, sets param_size and config_size (aligned to 64) and calls mdp_vpu_shared_mem_alloc, which allocates the DMA-coherent param, work and config buffers that are still NULL; on a failure there it frees the buffers recorded in vpu so far (including any that existed before this call), sets those pointers to NULL and returns -ENOMEM, which this function returns unchanged (it is not remapped from vpu->status). It then sends the INIT message again with the work buffer address and size and returns 0 if that succeeds, leaving the buffers allocated for the caller to release later. If either send fails the control reaches err_work_size: if vpu->status is -MDP_IPI_EBUSY the returned error is replaced by -EBUSY and if it is -MDP_IPI_ENOMEM by -ENOSPC (vpu->status is not reset by this function, so a stale value can remap an error from either send); otherwise the error from mdp_vpu_sendmsg is returned. If the second send fails the allocated buffers stay recorded in vpu and are not freed here. *lock is held only around the alignment and allocation and is released before any return.
note: Reviewer 1 right (an allocation failure returns -ENOMEM without status remapping, line 248); reviewer 2 right (stale vpu->status can remap a send error, 238-245); reviewer 3 right (mdp_vpu_ipi_handle_init_ack stores work_size and status even when the status is non-zero, mtk-mdp3-vpu.c:87-90, so work_size need not stay 0 after a failed first INIT). I did not verify the MDP_VPU_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT value (I wrote 'the message timeout', the earlier text said 500 ms) and left the number out. mdp_vpu_dev_init at 193-249.

name: vdec_msg_queue_wait_lat_buf_full
note: The listed item in vdec_msg_queue.h:181 is only a prototype (declaration with a kerneldoc comment), not a function body. The definition is vdec_msg_queue_wait_lat_buf_full in vdec_msg_queue.c:179-197: it returns true at once if lat_list_cnt equals NUM_BUFFER_COUNT (all lat buffers are in the lat list), otherwise it clears flush_done, queues the empty lat buffer on the core context, waits (wait_event, not interruptible) until flush_done, and returns false. The earlier reviewer was right that 'lat_list_cnt == NUM_BUFFER_COUNT' means all buffers are in the list, not idle, and that the old prose (blocks until then, returns true) was wrong. If the .c definition is queued as its own item it should use that description.

name: to_dw100_fmt_type
prose: Precondition: none; type may be any value of enum v4l2_buf_type (or any int). Postcondition: it returns DW100_FMT_OUTPUT (BIT(1), value 2) exactly when V4L2_TYPE_IS_OUTPUT(type) holds, that is when type is one of V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_OUTPUT (2), VBI_OUTPUT (5), SLICED_VBI_OUTPUT (7), VIDEO_OUTPUT_OVERLAY (8), VIDEO_OUTPUT_MPLANE (10), SDR_OUTPUT (12) or META_OUTPUT (14), and returns DW100_FMT_CAPTURE (BIT(0), value 1) for every other value, including V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_OVERLAY (3) and invalid values. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires 	rue; ensures result == ((type == 2 || type == 5 || type == 7 || type == 8 || type == 10 || type == 12 || type == 14) ? 2 : 1); */
note: Reviewer 4 right: V4L2_TYPE_IS_OUTPUT (videodev2.h:172-179) does not include type 3 (V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_OVERLAY); the old prose and contract listed 3. Reviewers 2 and 3 also right (not a range, includes 12 and 14). The exact set is 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14; DW100_FMT_CAPTURE = BIT(0), DW100_FMT_OUTPUT = BIT(1) (dw100.c:61-62). dw100.c:174-180.

name: imx8mq_mipi_csi_pm_resume
prose: Precondition: dev is a device whose driver data is a v4l2_subdev embedded in a valid csi_state (it is the system or runtime resume callback; state->lock is not held by the caller). Postcondition: it takes state->lock and releases it before returning. If ST_POWERED is clear it sets ST_POWERED first and then calls imx8mq_mipi_csi_clk_enable, so ST_POWERED stays set even if the clock enable fails. If ST_STREAMING is set it takes the active subdev state, calls imx8mq_mipi_csi_start_stream and releases the subdev state; this call's result replaces the result of the clock enable, so a failed clock enable is masked when the stream restart succeeds. If the restart fails it skips clearing ST_SUSPENDED (leaving it as it was) and returns -EAGAIN. Otherwise (not streaming, or the restart succeeded) it clears ST_SUSPENDED, including when the clock enable failed and the device was not streaming. It returns -EAGAIN if the last result that was stored is non-zero (the clock enable result when not streaming, or the stream restart result when streaming) and 0 otherwise.
note: Reviewer 1 right (ST_SUSPENDED not cleared if start_stream fails, goto unlock at 810-811); reviewer 2 right (a successful restart overwrites a failed clock enable); reviewer 3 right (ST_POWERED is set at 803 before clk_enable; failure leaves it set). Extra: with a failed clock enable and no streaming ST_SUSPENDED IS cleared (814) while -EAGAIN is returned. imx8mq-mipi-csi2.c:793-820.

name: size_vpss_line_buf_vpu33
prose: Precondition: the arithmetic is done in u32 with wraparound, so the caller must keep every intermediate value below 2^32; with 8192-pixel dimensions and up to 8 pipes the sums stay far below that, but values such as 1000 pipes and dimensions of 1,000,000 overflow (size_left alone is about 3.2e10). Postcondition: with max_wh = max(frame_width_coded, frame_height_coded), vpss_4tap_top = ((((max_wh*2)+3)>>2)<<4)+256, vpss_4tap_left = (((8192+3)>>2)<<5)+64, vpss_div2_top = (((max_wh+3)>>2)<<4)+256, vpss_div2_left = ((((max_wh*2)+3)>>2)<<5)+64, vpss_top_lb = (frame_width_coded+1)<<3, vpss_left_lb = (frame_height_coded<<3)*num_vpp_pipes_enc, size_left = (vpss_4tap_left+vpss_div2_left)*2*num_vpp_pipes_enc and size_top = (vpss_4tap_top+vpss_div2_top)*2, the result is size_left + size_top + vpss_top_lb + vpss_left_lb rounded up to a multiple of DMA_ALIGNMENT (256), computed in u32. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer right: the old precondition (pipes <= 1000, dims <= 1000000) permits u32 overflow in size_left (iris_vpu_buffer.c:863). Formula otherwise matches the code (847-867). DMA_ALIGNMENT is 256 (iris_vpu_buffer.h:13) and ALIGN masks, so it is correct for that power of two.

name: size_top_line_buf_first_stg_sao
prose: Precondition: frame_width_coded is at most 1000000 (so 16 * (frame_width_coded >> 5) fits easily in u32). Postcondition: the result is 16 * (frame_width_coded >> 5) rounded up to the next multiple of 256 (ALIGN with 256). It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:870-873 (ALIGN((16 * (w >> 5)), 256)); contract expands ALIGN as add-mask-and-clear, valid because 256 is a power of two.

name: size_enc_ref_buffer
prose: Precondition: frame_width and frame_height are small enough that the u32 products do not wrap (for example at most 10000). Postcondition: the result is (ALIGN(frame_height, 32) + ALIGN(frame_height >> 1, 32)) * ALIGN(frame_width, 32), where ALIGN rounds up to a multiple of 32. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:875-883 (luma height + chroma height of half the frame, each aligned to 32, times the aligned width).

name: size_enc_ten_bit_ref_buffer
prose: Precondition: frame_width and frame_height are small enough that the u32 products do not wrap (for example at most 10000). Postcondition: ref_luma_stride_in_bytes is frame_width rounded up to a multiple of SYSTEM_LAL_TILE10 (192); u_ref_stride = 4 * (that / 3) rounded up to a multiple of 128; ref_buf_height = frame_height rounded up to a multiple of 32; ref_chrm_height_in_bytes = ((frame_height + 1) >> 1) rounded up to a multiple of 32; luma_size = ref_buf_height * u_ref_stride rounded up to a multiple of 4096; chroma_size = u_ref_stride * ref_chrm_height_in_bytes rounded up to a multiple of 4096; the result is luma_size + chroma_size. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:886-905. Wording fix: the first step rounds frame_width up to a multiple of 192 with division and multiplication (SYSTEM_LAL_TILE10 = 192 is not a power of two so ALIGN would not be valid), the other roundings are masks on powers of two.

name: hfi_ubwc_calc_metadata_plane_stride
prose: Precondition: tile_width_in_pels > 0; metadata_stride_multiple is a power of two (ALIGN works by masking); frame_width + tile_width_in_pels - 1 and the aligned result do not wrap in u32 (for example frame_width <= 1000000, tile_width_in_pels <= 1000000, metadata_stride_multiple <= 1000000). Postcondition: the result is ceil(frame_width / tile_width_in_pels) = (frame_width + tile_width_in_pels - 1) / tile_width_in_pels, rounded up to a multiple of metadata_stride_multiple. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires tile_width_in_pels > 0 && frame_width <= 1000000 && tile_width_in_pels <= 1000000 && metadata_stride_multiple > 0 && metadata_stride_multiple <= 1000000 && (metadata_stride_multiple & (metadata_stride_multiple - 1)) == 0; ensures result == ((((frame_width + tile_width_in_pels - 1) / tile_width_in_pels) + metadata_stride_multiple - 1) & ~(metadata_stride_multiple - 1)); */
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:908-914 (ALIGN(ceil(w/tile), mult)). Added the power-of-two requirement: ALIGN is mask-based, so the old 'rounded up to a multiple' with an arbitrary multiple was not guaranteed and the contract mask expression was only valid for powers of two.

name: hfi_ubwc_metadata_plane_bufheight
prose: Precondition: tile_height_in_pels > 0; metadata_height_multiple is a power of two (ALIGN works by masking); frame_height + tile_height_in_pels - 1 and the aligned result do not wrap in u32 (for example frame_height <= 1000000, tile_height_in_pels <= 1000000, metadata_height_multiple <= 1000000). Postcondition: the result is ceil(frame_height / tile_height_in_pels) = (frame_height + tile_height_in_pels - 1) / tile_height_in_pels, rounded up to a multiple of metadata_height_multiple. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires tile_height_in_pels > 0 && frame_height <= 1000000 && tile_height_in_pels <= 1000000 && metadata_height_multiple > 0 && metadata_height_multiple <= 1000000 && (metadata_height_multiple & (metadata_height_multiple - 1)) == 0; ensures result == ((((frame_height + tile_height_in_pels - 1) / tile_height_in_pels) + metadata_height_multiple - 1) & ~(metadata_height_multiple - 1)); */
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:917-923. Same power-of-two correction as for the stride helper.

name: hfi_ubwc_metadata_plane_buffer_size
prose: Precondition: _metadata_tride * _metadata_buf_height does not wrap in u32 and, after rounding, stays below 2^32 (for example the product is at most 4000000000). Postcondition: the result is the product _metadata_tride * _metadata_buf_height rounded up to a multiple of 4096. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:926-929 (ALIGN(stride * height, 4096)).

name: hfi_buffer_non_comv_enc
prose: Precondition: lcu_size > 0 (it is a divisor), and the u32 intermediate products and the final sum do not wrap. Postcondition: with width_in_lcus = (frame_width + lcu_size - 1) / lcu_size, height_in_lcus = (frame_height + lcu_size - 1) / lcu_size, num_lcu_in_frame = width_in_lcus * height_in_lcus, frame_height_coded = height_in_lcus * lcu_size, frame_width_coded = width_in_lcus * lcu_size and num_lcumb = (frame_height_coded / lcu_size) * ((frame_width_coded + lcu_size * 8) / lcu_size), the result is size_enc_slice_info_buf(num_lcu_in_frame) + SIZE_SLICE_CMD_BUFFER + SIZE_SPS_PPS_SLICE_HDR + size_frame_rc_buf_size(standard, frame_height_coded, num_vpp_pipes_enc) + enc_bitcnt_buf_size(num_lcu_in_frame) + enc_bitmap_buf_size(num_lcu_in_frame) + SIZE_BSE_SLICE_CMD_BUF + SIZE_LAMBDA_LUT + size_override_buf(num_lcumb) + size_ir_buf(num_lcu_in_frame). It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Matches iris_vpu_buffer.c:932-956 term by term (order of the ten summands and the definition of num_lcumb checked). I did not read the called size helpers bodies.

name: hfi_buffer_line_enc_base
